title: Eomuk Bokkeum Stir-Fried Fish Cake
shortDescription: Prepared Korean fish cake is stir-fried with onion and carrot, then glazed with soy sauce, garlic, and rice syrup.
culturalContext: Eomuk bokkeum is a familiar Korean stir-fried fish-cake side dish. Fish-cake shape, vegetables, sweetness, chile, and sauce balance vary; this draft uses packaged sheets.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: label checked; cut into bite-size strips
allergenNotes: wheat/gluten; may contain egg, soy, shellfish, or other allergens

instructions.heading: Check and cut
instructions.action: Read the fish-cake package for allergens, storage, and heating directions; cut fish cake and vegetables on a clean board.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pieces are even and the label requirements are understood.
instructions.safetyNote: Fish cake formulas vary and may include fish, wheat, egg, soy, shellfish, or other allergens.

instructions.heading: Mix the glaze
instructions.action: Stir soy sauce, water, rice syrup, and garlic in a clean bowl.

instructions.heading: Stir-fry vegetables
instructions.action: Heat oil over medium-high and stir-fry onion and carrot until crisp-tender.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep the pan handle turned inward.

instructions.heading: Heat the fish cake
instructions.action: Add fish cake and stir-fry until hot and beginning to brown at the edges.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Fish cake is steaming throughout with light browning.
instructions.safetyNote: Follow any stricter package heating instruction.

instructions.heading: Glaze
instructions.action: Add the glaze and toss until reduced and glossy; remove from heat and add sesame oil and seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The sauce clings and no watery pool remains.
instructions.safetyNote: Reduced syrup is very hot; avoid splashing.

instructions.heading: Serve or chill
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean dish, rest 5 minutes, and serve warm or cool.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The glaze thickens slightly as it rests.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is stir-fried on the stovetop.
targetInternalTemperature: Follow the packaged fish cake manufacturer’s heating instructions; heat until steaming throughout.
visualDonenessCues: Glaze clings without a watery pool
foodSafetyNotes: Read and follow the packaged fish cake storage and heating instructions.
Fish cake formulas vary; verify fish, wheat/gluten, egg, soy, shellfish, and other allergen statements.
Heat until steaming throughout or to any stricter label direction.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains fish, wheat/gluten, soy, sesame, and potentially egg; packaged fish cake may also contain shellfish or other allergens, so the exact label controls.

substitutions: Use only a verified allergen-appropriate fish cake and adjust seasoning after test cooking.
ingredientSourcing: Buy refrigerated or frozen Korean fish cake from a high-turnover market.
Keep the original package so its ingredients, allergen statement, storage, and heating directions remain available.
makeAhead: Cut vegetables and mix glaze up to 1 day ahead; keep separately covered and refrigerated.
storage: Follow the package after-opening directions; refrigerate the cooked dish within 2 hours and use within 4 days or the stricter label window.
reheating: Reheat in a skillet until steaming throughout and follow any stricter package direction.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers in rice bowls within the approved or label-directed window.
servingSuggestions: Serve warm or cool as banchan.

faq.question: Are all Korean fish cakes the same?
faq.answer: No. Ingredients, texture, allergens, and heating directions vary by brand and product.

faq.question: Can I skip reading the label if fish is expected?
faq.answer: No. Fish cakes may contain wheat, egg, soy, shellfish, or other allergens.
